Example 5.4 — Build the evidence register and the diagnosis record

Task

Build the evidence register of case CASE-2026-016 (SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm, 256-bit) of 11 files), verify the integrity of the evidence, decide the category with the three questions, measure the scope and the exposure window, compute the priority after diagnosis, and write the diagnosis record outputs/A09_diagnosis_record.md and its machine-readable version outputs/a09_diagnosis.json.

Relation to the lecture

Part A of the script is the evidence register (5.4.8), part B the integrity verification and the one-letter demonstration (5.4.8), part C the three questions (5.4.2), part D the scope and the exposure window (5.4.4), part E the impact and the priority (5.4.5), part F the eleven sections of the record (5.4.7).

Future lab

Lab 3, Part C: the diagnosis of each of your two P1 (priority 1) items follows the same structure (template templates/C_diagnosis_template.md). Register and hash the evidence files that you use.

Why PowerShell

Atelier Nordik runs Windows, and Get-FileHash (Microsoft documentation) computes SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm, 256-bit) by default. The script runs in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and in PowerShell 7 on Windows, macOS and Linux (installation guide). Run it from the folder class16_files: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\New-DiagnosisRecord.ps1 (macOS or Linux: pwsh ./scripts/New-DiagnosisRecord.ps1). It needs the outputs of Example 5.3 and reads only the copies in a09_evidence.

Slide 34
scripts/New-DiagnosisRecord.ps1PowerShell · 357 lines
# =====================================================================================================# New-DiagnosisRecord.ps1 - Class 16, lesson 5.4 "Diagnosing incidents and documenting the findings"# Cyber.SoHo Educational Hub - educational material, (c) 2026 Cyber.SoHo / Asen Grozdanov.# TASK: turn the analysis of alert A-09 (lesson 5.3) into a documented diagnosis:# A register the evidence with SHA-256 hashes, B verify its integrity, C decide the category,# D measure the scope and the exposure window, E rate the impact and the priority,# F write the diagnosis record (Markdown) and a JSON file for lesson 5.5.# RELATION TO THE LECTURE: each function is one element of a diagnosis; the record has the same# sections as templates/C_diagnosis_template.md (Lab 3 Part C); the register lists the evidence and its hashes.# HOW TO RUN (Windows PowerShell 5.1 or PowerShell 7):# powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\New-DiagnosisRecord.ps1 (pwsh on macOS/Linux)# inputs : a09_evidence\ (11 files + collection_log.csv), a09_case\case_actions_2026-10-13.csv,# outputs\a09_findings.json and outputs\a09_timeline.csv (written by analyze_anomaly.py)# outputs: outputs\evidence_register.csv, outputs\A09_diagnosis_record.md, outputs\a09_diagnosis.json,# outputs\integrity_check.txt# Read-only on the evidence. Fictional data only; never run monitoring code on a system you are not# authorized to touch (Cyber.SoHo Legal Notice v2.0, sections 6.1 and 7.2).# ===================================================================================================== # Stop at the first error, so that a problem is never ignored silently.$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'# InvariantCulture writes dates and numbers the same way on every computer (fr-CA, en-CA, en-US...).$Inv = [System.Globalization.CultureInfo]::InvariantCulture# EDT (Eastern Daylight Time) is UTC minus 4 hours: the local time of Atelier Nordik in October.$EdtOffset = [TimeSpan]::FromHours(-4)# The folder that contains this script (the "scripts" folder of the downloads).$Here = $PSScriptRoot# The downloads folder is the parent folder of "scripts".$Root = Split-Path -Parent $Here# The evidence folder: this script reads it and never writes in it.$Evidence = Join-Path $Root 'a09_evidence'# The case folder: the actions log written by the technician during the case.$CaseDir = Join-Path $Root 'a09_case'# The outputs folder: results of lesson 5.3 and of this script.$Out = Join-Path $Root 'outputs'# The identifier of the case opened on Tuesday at 08:55.$CaseId = 'CASE-2026-016' # Helper: convert a time text of the evidence pack into a date-time in EDT.function ConvertTo-Edt { # The function receives one text, for example "2026-10-08T21:42:10Z" or "2026-10-13 09:02". param($Text) # If PowerShell already turned the text into a date, convert that date directly (the moment is kept). if ($Text -is [DateTimeOffset]) { return $Text.ToOffset($EdtOffset) } # Remove the spaces around the text. $t = ([string]$Text).Trim() # A text that contains "T" is an ISO 8601 time with an offset (or "Z" for UTC). if ($t -match 'T') { # DateTimeOffset keeps the offset written in the text, so UTC stays UTC until converted. $moment = [DateTimeOffset]::Parse($t, $Inv) # End of the 'if' block (the commands run only when the condition is true). } # Any other text is a local time written "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm". else { # Read the clock time in exactly that format, whatever the language of the computer. $clock = [DateTime]::ParseExact($t, 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm', $Inv) # Attach the EDT offset to that clock time. $moment = New-Object DateTimeOffset($clock, $EdtOffset) # End of the 'else' block. } # Express the moment in EDT, so that every time of the record uses the same time zone. return $moment.ToOffset($EdtOffset)# End of the function ConvertTo-Edt.} # Helper: format a moment as "Tue 2026-10-13 10:44" for the record.function Format-Edt { # The function receives one DateTimeOffset. param([DateTimeOffset]$Moment) # InvariantCulture gives English day names on every computer. return $Moment.ToString('ddd yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm', $Inv)# End of the function Format-Edt.} # A - REGISTER: hash every evidence file (SHA-256) and write the evidence register.function New-EvidenceRegister { # Print the title of the step. Write-Host 'A - REGISTER the evidence: SHA-256 hash, size, source, collector, time, method' # Read the collection log written while collecting (one line per evidence file). $log = Import-Csv -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Evidence 'collection_log.csv') -Encoding UTF8 # Prepare an empty list that will receive one register row per evidence file. $register = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object] # Process the evidence files one by one, in the order of the log. foreach ($item in $log) { # Build the full path of the evidence file. $path = Join-Path $Evidence $item.file # Compute the SHA-256 hash of the file: a 64-character value calculated from every byte; changing one byte changes it completely. $hash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $path -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant() # Read the size of the file in bytes, as a second simple check. $size = (Get-Item -LiteralPath $path).Length # Build the register row: what, from where, by whom, when, how, and the hash value. $row = [pscustomobject][ordered]@{ evidence_id = $item.evidence_id; file = $item.file; source_system = $item.source_system; independence_group = $item.independence_group; collected_by = $item.collected_by; collected_at_edt = $item.collected_at; method = $item.method; phase = $item.phase; size_bytes = $size; sha256 = $hash } # Add the row to the register. $register.Add($row) # Show the identifier, the first 16 characters of the hash and the file name. Write-Host (' {0} {1}... {2,6} bytes {3}' -f $item.evidence_id, $hash.Substring(0, 16), $size, $item.file) # End of the 'foreach' loop (the commands above run once per item). } # Save the register as CSV in the outputs folder (never in the evidence folder). $register | Export-Csv -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Out 'evidence_register.csv') -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8 # Give the register to the next steps. return $register# End of the function New-EvidenceRegister.} # B - VERIFY: hash the files again and compare; then show on a COPY why a hash detects any change.function Test-EvidenceIntegrity { # The function receives the register built in step A. param($Register) # Print the title of the step. Write-Host 'B - VERIFY integrity: hash again and compare with the register' # Prepare the lines of the integrity report. $report = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string] # Count the files whose hash matches. $ok = 0 # Check every file of the register. foreach ($row in $Register) { # Hash the file again, exactly as in step A. $again = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Evidence $row.file) -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant() # Compare the new hash with the registered hash. $same = ($again -eq $row.sha256) # Count the matches. if ($same) { $ok++ } # Write one line per file in the report. $report.Add(('{0} {1} {2}' -f $row.evidence_id, $(if ($same) { 'OK ' } else { 'MISMATCH' }), $row.file)) # End of the 'foreach' loop (the commands above run once per item). } # Print the result of the verification. Write-Host (' {0} of {1} files match their registered hash' -f $ok, $Register.Count) # Demonstration on a COPY of one evidence file (the original is never touched). $copy = Join-Path $Out 'tamper_demo_copy_of_E-08.csv' # Copy the maintenance calendar (E-08) to the outputs folder. Copy-Item -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Evidence 'maintenance_calendar.csv') -Destination $copy -Force # Read the copy as text. $text = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllText($copy) # Change one single character: the "N" of "Nightly" becomes "M". $changed = $text.Replace('Nightly', 'Mightly') # Write the modified text back into the copy. [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($copy, $changed) # Hash the original and the modified copy. $before = ($Register | Where-Object { $_.evidence_id -eq 'E-08' }).sha256 # Hash of the modified copy. $after = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $copy -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant() # Count how many of the 64 hexadecimal characters differ between the two hashes. $diff = 0 # Compare the two hashes character by character. for ($i = 0; $i -lt 64; $i++) { if ($before[$i] -ne $after[$i]) { $diff++ } } # Explain the demonstration in the report. $report.Add(('Demo on a copy: one character changed in E-08 -> {0} of 64 hash characters change' -f $diff)) # Show the two hashes one under the other. Write-Host (' demo on a copy of E-08: original {0}' -f $before) # The hash of the modified copy. Write-Host (' modified {0} ({1} of 64 characters differ)' -f $after, $diff) # Save the integrity report next to the register. Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Out 'integrity_check.txt') -Value $report -Encoding UTF8 # Return the number of matching files. return $ok# End of the function Test-EvidenceIntegrity.} # C - CATEGORY: answer the decision questions in order; the first "yes" decides.function Get-Category { # The function receives the findings of lesson 5.3 and the actions log. param($Findings, $Actions) # Print the title of the step. Write-Host 'C - DECIDE the category with the decision questions' # Look for the out-of-band confirmation (phone call to the contractor) in the actions log. $call = $Actions | Where-Object { $_.action -like 'Phone call to the IT contractor*' } | Select-Object -First 1 # Question 1: is there an actor without authorization, or a violation of policy? $q1 = -not ($Findings.techniques_tested[0].result -like 'NOT SUPPORTED*' -and $null -ne $call) # Question 2: does a monitoring or protection tool fail to see or to protect? $q2 = ($Findings.category -eq 'monitoring failure') # The first question answered "yes" gives the category. if ($q1) { $category = 'Security incident' } elseif ($q2) { $category = 'Monitoring failure' } else { $category = 'Benign' } # Write the reasoning, so that a reader can check every answer. $reason = @(('Q1 unauthorized actor or policy violation? {0} - change made by contractor-it from 203.0.113.150 under approved ticket CH-2026-090; confirmed by phone {1} ({2})' -f $(if ($q1) { 'YES' } else { 'NO' }), $call.time, $call.result), ('Q2 monitoring or protection tool failing? {0} - definitions not updated on three workstations since Thursday 17:15' -f $(if ($q2) { 'YES' } else { 'NO' }))) # Print the reasoning and the category. foreach ($line in $reason) { Write-Host (' ' + $line) } # Print the decision. Write-Host (' -> category: {0}' -f $category) # Return the category and its reasoning. return [pscustomobject]@{ Category = $category; Reason = $reason; Call = $call }# End of the function Get-Category.} # D - SCOPE: which assets, accounts and data; when the exposure started and when it ended.function Get-Scope { # The function receives the findings of lesson 5.3. param($Findings) # Print the title of the step. Write-Host 'D - MEASURE the scope and the exposure window' # Read the events collected before the fix (E-05): the evidence itself gives the start of the exposure. $before = Import-Csv -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Evidence 'ws-render_defender-events_2026-10-08_13.csv') -Encoding UTF8 # The exposure started with the FIRST failed update (event 2001) of the three workstations. $start = ($before | Where-Object { $_.EventId -eq '2001' } | ForEach-Object { ConvertTo-Edt $_.TimeCreated } | Sort-Object -Property UtcDateTime | Select-Object -First 1) # Read the events collected after the fix (E-09). $after = Import-Csv -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Evidence 'ws-render_defender-events_after-fix_2026-10-13.csv') -Encoding UTF8 # Keep the successful updates (event 2000) of the three workstations. $updates = $after | Where-Object { $_.EventId -eq '2000' } # The exposure ends when the LAST of the three workstations is updated. $end = ($updates | ForEach-Object { ConvertTo-Edt $_.TimeCreated } | Sort-Object -Property UtcDateTime | Select-Object -Last 1) # The length of the exposure window. $length = $end - $start # Write the length in days, hours and minutes. $text = '{0} days {1} h {2} min' -f $length.Days, $length.Hours, $length.Minutes # Read the console status after the fix (E-11) to confirm that the scans found nothing. $status = Import-Csv -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Evidence 'av-console_device-status_after-fix_2026-10-13.csv') -Encoding UTF8 # Add the threats found by the three full scans. $threats = [int](($status | Measure-Object -Property threats_found -Sum).Sum) # Read the new definition version reported after the fix. $version = ($updates | Select-Object -First 1).CurrentVersion # Print the scope. Write-Host ' assets: WS-10-22, WS-10-37, WS-10-51 | accounts: none | data: none accessed' # Print the exposure window. Write-Host (' exposure: {0} -> {1} ({2})' -f (Format-Edt $start), (Format-Edt $end), $text) # Print the verification of the recovery. Write-Host (' verified: definitions {0} on the three workstations; full scans: {1} threat(s)' -f $version, $threats) # Return everything the record needs. return [pscustomobject]@{ Start = $start; End = $end; Text = $text; Threats = $threats; Version = $version }# End of the function Get-Scope.} # E - IMPACT AND PRIORITY: rate confidentiality, integrity, availability, then compute the priority.function Get-Priority { # The function receives the impact rating of the assets and the confidence that the problem is real. param([int]$Impact, [int]$Confidence) # Print the title of the step. Write-Host 'E - RATE the impact (CIA) and compute the priority (same scale as lesson 5.2)' # Priority score = impact x confidence, as in the triage of Class 15. $score = $Impact * $Confidence # Translate the score into a band: P1 16 or more, P2 10 to 15, P3 5 to 9, P4 4 or less. if ($score -ge 16) { $band = 'P1' } elseif ($score -ge 10) { $band = 'P2' } elseif ($score -ge 5) { $band = 'P3' } else { $band = 'P4' } # Print the impact on each property of information. Write-Host ' confidentiality: none observed | integrity: potential (old definitions) | availability: none observed' # Print the priority after diagnosis. Write-Host (' priority: impact {0} x confidence {1} = {2} -> {3} (triage had P3)' -f $Impact, $Confidence, $score, $band) # Return the score and the band. return [pscustomobject]@{ Score = $score; Band = $band }# End of the function Get-Priority.} # F - RECORD: write the diagnosis record (Markdown) and the JSON file used by lesson 5.5.function Write-DiagnosisRecord { # The function receives everything computed by the previous steps. param($Findings, $Register, $Decision, $Scope, $Priority, $Actions, $Timeline) # Print the title of the step. Write-Host 'F - WRITE the diagnosis record and the JSON file for lesson 5.5' # The record is built line by line in a list. $md = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string] # Title of the record. $md.Add(('# Diagnosis record - {0} (alert A-09)' -f $CaseId)) # Classification of the record itself: internal, need-to-know. $md.Add('TLP:AMBER+STRICT - Atelier Nordik inc. only (fictional). Status: closed - recovered and verified. Analyst: technician. Written: Tue 2026-10-13 12:30 EDT.') # Section 1: the facts in a few sentences. $md.Add(''); $md.Add('## 1. What happened (facts)') # The summary from lesson 5.3. $md.Add($Findings.summary) # Section 2: the category and the reasoning that led to it. $md.Add(''); $md.Add(('## 2. Category: {0}' -f $Decision.Category)) # One line per decision question. foreach ($line in $Decision.Reason) { $md.Add('- ' + $line) } # Section 3: the root cause. $md.Add(''); $md.Add('## 3. Root cause') # The cause that, once removed, prevents the problem from coming back. $md.Add('Change CH-2026-090 had three steps. Step 2 (point policy Render-WS to \\SRV-AD01\AVDefs, no fallback) was applied on Thu 17:42; step 1 (create that share and its copy job, planned Fri 09:00) was never done; the ticket had no verification step and was not entered in the maintenance calendar.') # Section 4: scope and exposure window. $md.Add(''); $md.Add('## 4. Scope and exposure window') # Assets, accounts and data concerned. $md.Add('- Assets: WS-10-22, WS-10-37, WS-10-51 (rendering workstations, criticality 2). Accounts: none. Data: no personal or client information accessed, used, sent or lost.') # The exposure window measured from the evidence. $md.Add(('- Exposure window: {0} -> {1} EDT ({2}) without new definitions.' -f (Format-Edt $Scope.Start), (Format-Edt $Scope.End), $Scope.Text)) # Section 5: impact and priority. $md.Add(''); $md.Add('## 5. Impact (CIA) and priority') # The three properties of information, one by one. $md.Add('- Confidentiality: none observed. Integrity: potential (a new threat would not have been recognized). Availability: none observed.') # The priority before and after diagnosis. $md.Add(('- Priority: triage P3 (score 6) -> after diagnosis {0} (score {1}); the gap was real, so it was fixed the same morning.' -f $Priority.Band, $Priority.Score)) # Section 6: adversary behaviour. $md.Add(''); $md.Add('## 6. Adversary behaviour (MITRE ATT&CK)') # No technique is assigned; the tested technique and its result are written anyway. $md.Add(('- None assigned. Tested: {0} {1} ({2}) - refuted: change confirmed by the contractor by phone at {3}.' -f $Findings.techniques_tested[0].id, $Findings.techniques_tested[0].name, $Findings.techniques_tested[0].tactic, $Decision.Call.time)) # Section 7: confidence. $md.Add(''); $md.Add('## 7. Confidence: high') # Why the confidence is high. $md.Add(('- {0} independent groups agree (workstations, console, SRV-AD01, change log); no record contradicts the conclusion; the fix removed the symptom.' -f $Findings.independent_groups)) # Section 8: key timeline, with references to the evidence (file and line). $md.Add(''); $md.Add('## 8. Key timeline (EDT) - full timeline in a09_timeline.csv') # Table header. $md.Add('| Time (EDT) | Evidence | Line | Interpretation |'); $md.Add('|---|---|---|---|') # Keep the key rows: last success, change, first failure, alert, last failure, missing share. foreach ($row in ($Timeline | Where-Object { $_.interpretation -match 'event 2000, last success|CH-2026-090|FIRST failure|Alert A-09|LAST failure|does not exist' })) { $md.Add(('| {0} | {1} | {2} | {3} |' -f $row.time_edt, $row.evidence_id, $row.line, $row.interpretation)) } # Section 9: the actions log, written while working (contemporaneous notes). $md.Add(''); $md.Add('## 9. Actions taken (contemporaneous log)') # One line per action, with who did it and the result. foreach ($a in $Actions) { $md.Add(('- {0} - {1}: {2} -> {3}' -f $a.time, $a.who, $a.action, $a.result)) } # Section 10: the evidence register with the hashes. $md.Add(''); $md.Add('## 10. Evidence register (SHA-256) - full register in evidence_register.csv') # Table header. $md.Add('| ID | File | Collected (EDT) | SHA-256 (first 16) |'); $md.Add('|---|---|---|---|') # One row per evidence file. foreach ($r in $Register) { $md.Add(('| {0} | {1} | {2} | {3} |' -f $r.evidence_id, $r.file, $r.collected_at_edt, $r.sha256.Substring(0, 16))) } # Section 11: what remains open, and the lessons proposed for the review of Friday. $md.Add(''); $md.Add('## 11. Open questions and lessons learned (review: Fri 2026-10-16)') # The process questions that the review must answer. $md.Add('- Open: why step 1 was skipped; whether the rendering policy should keep a file share at all (owner decision).') # Lesson 1: a verification step in every change. $md.Add('- Lesson 1: every change ticket states, before the change, how its success will be verified.') # Lesson 2: the maintenance calendar must contain every change. $md.Add('- Lesson 2: every change is entered in the maintenance calendar used by triage.') # Lesson 3: a fallback to the publisher. $md.Add('- Lesson 3: a policy that changes the update source keeps the publisher service as a fallback.') # Lesson 4: faster alert (tuning, Topic 6.4). $md.Add('- Lesson 4 (Topic 6.4): alert after two consecutive failed updates (8 hours) instead of waiting for the daily check (more than 24 hours without a successful update).') # The label again at the bottom of the record (TLP 2.0: in the header and the footer of the document). $md.Add(''); $md.Add('TLP:AMBER+STRICT - Atelier Nordik inc. only.') # Save the record in UTF-8. Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Out 'A09_diagnosis_record.md') -Value $md -Encoding UTF8 # Build the JSON object used by build_report.py (lesson 5.5). $json = [ordered]@{ case_id = $CaseId; alert = 'A-09'; category = $Decision.Category; what_happened = $Findings.summary; root_cause = 'Change CH-2026-090: step 2 applied without step 1 (the share was never created); no verification step; not in the maintenance calendar'; assets = @('WS-10-22', 'WS-10-37', 'WS-10-51'); personal_information_involved = $false; exposure_start = $Scope.Start.ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:sszzz', $Inv); exposure_end = $Scope.End.ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:sszzz', $Inv); exposure_text = $Scope.Text; impact = [ordered]@{ confidentiality = 'none observed'; integrity = 'potential'; availability = 'none observed' }; priority_triage = 'P3'; priority_after = $Priority.Band; priority_score = $Priority.Score; attack_technique = $null; technique_tested = $Findings.techniques_tested[0].id + ' ' + $Findings.techniques_tested[0].name; confidence = 'high'; definitions_after_fix = $Scope.Version; threats_found = $Scope.Threats; actions = @($Actions); evidence = @($Register | Select-Object evidence_id, file, sha256); lessons = @('Verification step in every change ticket', 'Every change in the maintenance calendar', 'Keep the publisher service as fallback', 'Alert after two consecutive failed updates') } # Write the JSON file (depth 5 keeps the nested lists). Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Out 'a09_diagnosis.json') -Value ($json | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5) -Encoding UTF8 # Confirm where the files are. Write-Host (' saved: {0}, a09_diagnosis.json, evidence_register.csv, integrity_check.txt' -f (Join-Path $Out 'A09_diagnosis_record.md'))# End of the function Write-DiagnosisRecord.} # MAIN: run the six steps in order.# The findings must exist: they are written by analyze_anomaly.py (lesson 5.3).if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Out 'a09_findings.json'))) { throw 'Run scripts/analyze_anomaly.py first (lesson 5.3): outputs/a09_findings.json is missing.' }# Read the findings of lesson 5.3 (JSON text -> object).$findings = Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Out 'a09_findings.json') -Raw -Encoding UTF8 | ConvertFrom-Json# Read the timeline of lesson 5.3.$timeline = Import-Csv -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Out 'a09_timeline.csv') -Encoding UTF8# Read the actions log of the case.$actions = Import-Csv -LiteralPath (Join-Path $CaseDir 'case_actions_2026-10-13.csv') -Encoding UTF8# Step A: register the evidence.$register = New-EvidenceRegister# Step B: verify the integrity.$null = Test-EvidenceIntegrity -Register $register# Step C: decide the category.$decision = Get-Category -Findings $findings -Actions $actions# Step D: measure the scope and the exposure window.$scope = Get-Scope -Findings $findings# Step E: impact 2 (workstations, as in triage) and confidence 5 (the gap is confirmed).$priority = Get-Priority -Impact 2 -Confidence 5# Step F: write the record and the JSON file.Write-DiagnosisRecord -Findings $findings -Register $register -Decision $decision -Scope $scope -Priority $priority -Actions $actions -Timeline $timeline
Ready

The simulator replays the real output of the script, line by line, on the embedded evidence pack. Start and Pause control the replay; Pause keeps the position, and Start resumes from that step; Restart clears everything. While paused, click any line of the execution window to see which part of the code produced it. The register hashes are recomputed by your browser from the embedded files.

Step-by-step explanation of New-DiagnosisRecord.ps1

  1. Preparation. The script stops at the first error, keeps the invariant culture in $Inv so that dates are read and written the same way on French and English computers, defines the folders and the EDT (Eastern Daylight Time) offset; its main part, at the bottom of the file, reads the findings of Example 5.3 (a09_findings.json), the timeline and the actions log, and calls the functions A to F in order.
  2. Time helpers. ConvertTo-Edt converts any time of the pack to EDT (Eastern Daylight Time); Format-Edt writes it as "Thu 2026-10-08 17:42".
  3. A, register. New-EvidenceRegister runs Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 on each file listed in collection_log.csv and writes outputs/evidence_register.csv with the hash, the size, the source, the collector, the time and the method.
  4. B, verify. Test-EvidenceIntegrity computes every hash again and compares it with the register (11 of 11 match). It then copies E-08, changes one letter in the copy only, and counts how many characters of the hash changed (60 of 64).
  5. C, category. Get-Category answers Question 1 from the actions log (phone confirmation at 09:50) and Question 2 from the findings (definitions not updated): monitoring failure.
  6. D, scope. Get-Scope takes the start of the exposure from the first event 2001 in E-05 and its end from the last event 2000 in E-09, and reads the definition version and the threats found after the fix.
  7. E, priority. Get-Priority multiplies impact 2 by confidence 5 and maps the score 10 to P2 (priority 2) with the bands of lesson 5.2.
  8. F, record. Write-DiagnosisRecord writes the eleven sections in Markdown and the same content as JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) for lesson 5.5.

5.5

Communicating results to the people concerned

Slide 36

A correct diagnosis that reaches the wrong person, too late, or in words the reader cannot use, changes nothing. Communication is part of the competency: effective communication with stakeholders is a performance criterion of EZ01, and the NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology) Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 defines it as a category of the Respond function, Incident Response Reporting and Communication (RS.CO): "response activities are coordinated with internal and external stakeholders as required by laws, regulations, or policies".

Slide 37

5.5.1 Key terms

Stakeholder
A person or an organization that is affected by the problem, must act on it, or must be informed of it by law.
Need-to-know
The rule that a person receives a piece of information only if they need it to do their part. It protects the people whose data appear in the evidence, and it avoids alarming people who cannot act.
Out-of-band communication
Communication through a channel that is separate from the systems under investigation, for example a phone call to a number taken from the contract instead of an e-mail, when the e-mail account could be controlled by an intruder.
Communication record
The list of who was informed, of what, when, by whom, through which channel and under which label, and of who was deliberately not informed, with the reason.
Plain language
Writing that the intended reader can understand the first time they read it.
Slide 38

5.5.2 Who needs to know

  • List the stakeholders by role: the decision maker (the owner), the people who fix the problem (the IT (information technology) contractor), the people affected (users of the three workstations), the people who might be affected (other staff, clients) and the authorities (privacy regulators, the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, the police).
  • For each one, decide yes or no and write the reason. A "no" is a decision too, and it must be possible to check it later.
  • A-09: three recipients (the owner, the contractor, the users of the three rendering workstations) and six deliberate non-recipients (other staff, clients, the Commission d'accès à l'information, the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada, the Cyber Centre, the police), each with its reason.

5.5.3 Labels: the Traffic Light Protocol

The Traffic Light Protocol, version 2.0, published by the Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams in August 2022, is a set of labels that tell the recipient how far they may share a piece of information. In a document, the label is written in the header and the footer of every page; in an e-mail, it is written in the subject line and directly before the labelled information.

Table 5.5-2 - Traffic Light Protocol (TLP) 2.0 labels
LabelWho may receive the informationUse in case A-09
TLP:RED (Traffic Light Protocol)Only the individual recipients; no further disclosureNot used
TLP:AMBER+STRICT (Traffic Light Protocol)Only members of the recipient's own organizationOwner note and diagnosis record (Atelier Nordik only)
TLP:AMBER (Traffic Light Protocol)The recipient's organization and its clients, on a need-to-know basisTechnical annex sent to the IT (information technology) contractor
TLP:GREEN (Traffic Light Protocol)The community (peers and partners), not public channelsMessage to the users of the rendering computers
TLP:CLEAR (Traffic Light Protocol)Anyone; no limit except copyrightNot used: nothing of this case is public
Source: Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams (FIRST), TLP (Traffic Light Protocol) version 2.0, August 2022. Documents: label in the header and the footer of every page. E-mail: label in the subject line and just before the information.

A-09: the owner note and the diagnosis record carry TLP:AMBER+STRICT (Traffic Light Protocol) (Atelier Nordik only). The technical annex carries TLP:AMBER (Traffic Light Protocol): the contractor may share it inside its own firm and, on a need-to-know basis, with its clients, for example to check whether another client has the same setting. The users' message contains nothing that could help an intruder and carries TLP:GREEN (Traffic Light Protocol). Monitoring data stay confidential in every case: respect for the confidentiality of the monitoring data collected is a performance criterion of EZ01 (Legal Notice, section 7.2).

Slide 40

5.5.4 When and how

  • Timing follows priority (lesson 5.2): P1 (priority 1) now, P2 (priority 2) today, P3 (priority 3) this week. A-09 became P2 (priority 2) at 09:40: the owner was called at 10:05 and received the written note at 13:00.
  • Speak before you act, write after you verify. A decision that changes a system, here reverting the policy, is agreed by phone with the person who has the authority (the owner) and the person who will make the change (the contractor). The written messages are sent after the fix has been verified (the last full scan ended at 12:20), so that they contain verified facts.
  • Out of band. The contractor was called at the number written in the service contract, not at a number found in an e-mail or in the console. If hypothesis H4 had been true, an intruder holding the console account or a mailbox could have answered in the contractor's place.
  • Every conversation is recorded in the actions log at the time it happens: time, person, what was said, decision.
Slide 41

5.5.5 One set of facts, four audiences

All messages are written from a single source of facts, the diagnosis record. Only the vocabulary, the level of detail and the channel change. Two versions of the facts would sooner or later contradict each other.

AudienceWhat they needLanguageLength and formatChannelA-09 example
Owner (decision maker)What happened, what it could cost, what was done, what she must decide, what happens nextPlain language: no abbreviation, no host name, no code; short sentencesOne pagePhone first, then the written note"The three rendering computers did not get antivirus updates."
IT (information technology) contractor (technical)Timeline, evidence references (file, line, hash), actions in priority orderTechnical: identifiers, codes, versionsTechnical annex with tablesPhone at the contract number, then the annex"Event 2001, File share \\SRV-AD01\AVDefs, error 0x80070035."
Users affectedWhat happened, that no action is needed, what not to do, whom to callPlain and short3 to 5 sentencesShort message"You do not need to do anything."
Authorities (when required)The content that the law requires, nothing morePrecise and factualThe official formThe regulator's form or portalNot required for A-09 (no personal information accessed, used, communicated or lost)
Same facts for everyone; only the words, the detail and the channel change.
Slide 42

5.5.6 The note for the owner: plain language

  • Five parts: what happened; what it could have cost; what was done; what we need from you (each decision with a date); what happens next.
  • Rules from the Canada.ca Content Style Guide of the Government of Canada: short sentences (the guide gives under 15 to 20 words as the optimum); one idea per sentence; active voice ("our computer support company changed the setting back", not "the setting was changed back"); short, everyday words; abbreviations avoided unless they are necessary; dates such as "October 13" and times such as "10:46 am". Our own rules for the owner note: no host names, ticket numbers or error codes; the day written with the date and the time ("Tuesday, October 13 at 10:46 am"); every number with its unit; no sentence longer than 25 words (the script refuses longer ones).
  • Facts without blame. Describe what happened and what will change; do not judge people.
  • Honest uncertainty. If something is not known yet, write it and say when it will be known.

Slide 43

The same facts for two readers

The left column is useful to the person who makes the fix: it identifies the computers, the error, the evidence. The right column is useful to the person who decides: it says what happened, what it could have cost, what was done and what she must decide, without a single abbreviation or identifier.

Slide 44

5.5.7 The technical annex

  • It is written for the person who makes the fix: identifiers, codes, versions, and evidence references (file, line, SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm, 256-bit)).
  • It follows the phases of the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security guide ITSAP.40.003 (publication 40.003 of the Information Technology Security Awareness series of the Cyber Centre), Developing your incident response plan. Preparation happens before the incident, so the annex starts with detection and analysis, then containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident activities and lessons learned, in that order; within each phase, actions are listed by priority.
  • A-09: containment not required (no attacker; real-time protection stayed on); eradication: policy reverted at 10:30 (E-10); recovery verified: definitions 1.441.702.0 installed from 10:44 to 10:46 (E-09), full scans with 0 threats (E-09, E-11); four lessons for the review of Friday, October 16: a verification step in every change ticket, every change in the maintenance calendar, the publisher's service kept as a fallback source, and an alert after two consecutive failed updates.
Slide 45

5.5.8 Notification duties in Québec and in Canada

This part is general information, not legal advice (Legal Notice, section 16). In a real case the decision belongs to the person in charge, with legal counsel when the answer is not clear; the technician prepares the facts.

Law 25 is the common name of the Québec law of 2021 that modernized the protection of personal information. For an enterprise such as Atelier Nordik, it amended the Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector (CQLR (Compilation of Québec Laws and Regulations), chapter P-39.1):

  • Section 3.1: the person exercising the highest authority in the enterprise (here, the owner) is the person in charge of the protection of personal information, unless the function is delegated in writing.
  • Section 3.6: a confidentiality incident is the access, use or communication of personal information not authorized by law, its loss, or any other breach of its protection.
  • Section 3.5: when the enterprise has reason to believe that such an incident occurred, it takes reasonable measures to reduce the risk of injury; if the incident presents a risk of serious injury, it must promptly notify the Commission d'accès à l'information and the persons concerned.
  • Section 3.7: the risk is assessed from the sensitivity of the information, the anticipated consequences of its use and the likelihood that it will be used for injurious purposes, in consultation with the person in charge.
  • Section 3.8 and the Regulation respecting confidentiality incidents (sections 7 and 8): every confidentiality incident goes into a register, kept at least 5 years, which includes the reasoning on the risk of serious injury.

A-09: was personal information accessed, used, communicated or lost? No. It is therefore not a confidentiality incident: no notice and no register entry, and the reasoning is kept in the case file (A09_notification_decision.md).

Slide 46

The other three checks

  • PIPEDA (Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act) (federal law): in Québec it applies mainly to federally regulated businesses (banks, telecommunications, airlines) and to personal information that crosses provincial or national borders in commercial activities. A breach of security safeguards involving personal information that creates a real risk of significant harm must be reported to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada and to the individuals, as soon as feasible. Organizations that can reduce the harm must also be notified. Every breach is recorded, and the record is kept 24 months (Breach of Security Safeguards Regulations).
  • Canadian Centre for Cyber Security: businesses may report a cyber incident through the official reporting page. The report is voluntary for a private business; it helps warn others and gives access to advice.
  • Police: when a crime is suspected, for example the unauthorized use of a computer (Criminal Code, section 342.1). In an emergency, call 911. To report a non-urgent crime in Montréal, contact the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal.
  • A-09: "no" to all four checks, each with its reason recorded:

Example 5.5 — Write the messages from one set of facts

Task

From the diagnosis of lesson 5.4 (outputs/a09_diagnosis.json), decide the legal notifications and record the reasoning, choose the audiences with their channel, time and label, write the owner note in plain language and check it automatically, write the technical annex in the order of ITSAP.40.003 (publication 40.003 of the Information Technology Security Awareness series of the Cyber Centre), and save the communication record.

Relation to the lecture

Step 2 of the script is section 5.5.8 (law), step 3 is 5.5.2 to 5.5.4 (who, label, channel, time), step 4 is 5.5.6 (plain language, with an automatic check of abbreviations and sentence length), step 5 is 5.5.7 (annex), step 6 writes the communication record.

Future lab

Lab 3, Part D asks for exactly these two documents for your two P1 (priority 1) items: one page for the owner, in plain language, and a technical annex for the IT (information technology) contractor, in ITSAP.40.003 (publication 40.003 of the Information Technology Security Awareness series of the Cyber Centre) order (D_report.md; template templates/D_report_template.md).

Run it yourself

After Examples 5.3 and 5.4: python3 scripts/build_report.py (Windows: py scripts\build_report.py). The five files appear in outputs/.

Fictional data only (Cyber.SoHo Legal Notice v2.0, sections 6.7 and 7.2).# ===================================================================================================== # Import csv: it reads the stakeholder list, the glossary, the timeline and the evidence register.import csv# Import json: the diagnosis written by the PowerShell script of lesson 5.4 is a JSON file.import json# Import re (regular expressions): it finds abbreviations and identifiers that an owner would not understand.import re# Import datetime: the times of the diagnosis are turned into plain words ("Tuesday, October 13 at 10:46 am").from datetime import datetime# Import Path: it builds file paths that work on Windows, macOS and Linux.from pathlib import Path # The folder of this script ("scripts").HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent# The downloads folder, parent of "scripts".ROOT = HERE.parent# The folder with the results of lessons 5.3 and 5.4; this script writes its messages there too.OUT = ROOT / "outputs"# The folder with the case inputs (stakeholders and plain-language glossary).CASE = ROOT / "a09_case"# A pattern that finds what an owner would not understand: UNC paths, hexadecimal codes,# identifiers with digits (WS-10-22, CH-2026-090, P2, T1685, SHA-256) and words written in capitals (IT, EDT).JARGON = re.compile(r"\\\\\S+|\b0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+\b|\b[A-Z]{1,5}-?\d[\w.\-]*\b|\b[A-Z]{2,}\b")# Plain-language rule taken from the Canada.ca Content Style Guide: keep sentences short.MAX_WORDS = 25 # Helper: read a CSV file and return its rows as dictionaries ("utf-8-sig" also accepts the BOM of PowerShell 5.1).def read_csv(path): # Open the file in read-only mode. with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as handle: # Return every row, with the header as keys. return list(csv.DictReader(handle)) # Helper: write a time in plain words, for example "Tuesday, October 13 at 10:46 am".def plain_time(iso_text): # Read the ISO 8601 text written by the PowerShell script (local time with its offset). moment = datetime.fromisoformat(iso_text) # Write the hour on a 12-hour clock without a leading zero, as the Canada.ca guide recommends. hour = moment.strftime("%I").lstrip("0") + moment.strftime(":%M ") + ("am" if moment.hour < 12 else "pm") # Return the weekday, the month, the day and the hour. return f"{moment.strftime('%A')}, {moment.strftime('%B')} {moment.day} at {hour}" # STEP 1 - FACTS: read the single source of facts; every message below is written from it.def step1_facts(): # Print the title of the step. print("STEP 1 - READ the facts (one source for every message: the diagnosis of lesson 5.4)") # Read the diagnosis written by New-DiagnosisRecord.ps1. facts = json.loads((OUT / "a09_diagnosis.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")) # Show the facts that every audience will receive, each in its own words. print(f" {facts['case_id']}: {facts['category']}; exposure {facts['exposure_text']}; priority {facts['priority_triage']} -> {facts['priority_after']}; personal information involved: {facts['personal_information_involved']}") # Give the facts to the next steps. return facts # STEP 2 - LAW: decide which notifications the law requires, and write down why (even when the answer is "no").def step2_notifications(facts): # Print the title of the step. print("STEP 2 - DECIDE the notifications required by law, and record the reasoning") # Personal information involved? This single fact decides the two privacy laws. personal = facts["personal_information_involved"] # An attack or a crime? A monitoring failure has no attacker. attack = facts["category"] == "Security incident" # Prepare the list of decisions. decisions = [] # Québec, Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector (as amended by Law 25), s. 3.5 to 3.8. decisions.append({"rule": "Québec private-sector Act (amended by Law 25), s. 3.5-3.8", "question": "Confidentiality incident (access, use, communication or loss of personal information)?", "answer": "yes" if personal else "no", "consequence": "Assess the risk of serious injury; if serious: notify the CAI and the persons; always: enter it in the register (kept 5 years)" if personal else "Not a confidentiality incident: no notice to the CAI or to persons, no register entry"}) # Canada, PIPEDA, breach of security safeguards (applies to some cross-border situations). decisions.append({"rule": "PIPEDA, breach of security safeguards", "question": "Breach involving personal information with a real risk of significant harm?", "answer": "yes" if personal else "no", "consequence": "Report to the OPC, notify individuals, keep a record 24 months" if personal else "No breach of security safeguards: nothing to report or record"}) # Canadian Centre for Cyber Security: voluntary reporting of cyber incidents by businesses. decisions.append({"rule": "Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (voluntary report)", "question": "Cyber attack or attempt worth sharing?", "answer": "yes" if attack else "no", "consequence": "Report through the Cyber Centre online form" if attack else "No attack: nothing to report"}) # Police: only when a crime is suspected (for example Criminal Code s. 342.1, unauthorized use of a computer). decisions.append({"rule": "Police (Criminal Code s. 342.1 and others)", "question": "Crime suspected?", "answer": "yes" if attack else "no", "consequence": "Call the police with the case number and preserve the evidence" if attack else "No crime: no report"}) # Print one line per decision. for item in decisions: # Law, answer, consequence. print(f" {item['rule']:<58} -> {item['answer']:<3} | {item['consequence']}") # Give the decisions to the next steps. return decisions # STEP 3 - AUDIENCES: inform the people who need to know, and only them; record why the others are not informed.def step3_audiences(): # Print the title of the step. print("STEP 3 - CHOOSE the audiences (need-to-know) and their channel, time and TLP label") # Read the list of stakeholders prepared for the case. people = read_csv(CASE / "stakeholders.csv") # Print who receives a message and who does not, with the reason. for person in people: # The TLP (Traffic Light Protocol) label says how far the message may be shared. print(f" {'INFORM ' if person['needs_to_know'] == 'yes' else 'no msg '} {person['stakeholder']:<52} {person['channel']:<46} {person['tlp']}") # Give the list to the next steps. return people # STEP 4 - OWNER NOTE: the same facts, in plain words; then check the plain-language rules automatically.def step4_owner_note(facts): # Print the title of the step. print("STEP 4 - WRITE the owner note in plain language and CHECK it") # Read the glossary: each technical term and the plain words that replace it. glossary = read_csv(CASE / "plain_language.csv") # The start and the end of the exposure, in plain words. start, end = plain_time(facts["exposure_start"]), plain_time(facts["exposure_end"]) # Each pair is (technical sentence written from the facts, plain sentence written from the same facts). pairs = [] # Fact 1: what happened. pairs.append((f"WS-10-22, WS-10-37 and WS-10-51 did not update their antivirus definitions from {facts['exposure_start']} to {facts['exposure_end']} (exposure window {facts['exposure_text']}).", f"From {start} to {end}, the three rendering computers did not get antivirus updates. These updates bring the list of known threats.")) # Fact 2: why it happened. pairs.append(("Root cause: CH-2026-090 set policy Render-WS to \\\\SRV-AD01\\AVDefs without fallback; step 1 (create the share) was never done.", "A setting changed on Thursday told these computers to get that list from a shared folder on our main server. That folder was never created.")) # Fact 3: the category. pairs.append((f"Category: {facts['category']}; T1685 tested and refuted; no IoC.", "This was a mistake in a planned change. It was not an attack.")) # Fact 4: what it could have cost. pairs.append(("CIA impact: C none, I potential, A none.", "For four and a half days, a new threat could have reached these computers without being recognized. Nobody saw, changed or lost our files or our clients' information.")) # Fact 5: what was done. pairs.append((f"Recovery: policy reverted 10:30, definitions {facts['definitions_after_fix']} at 10:46, full scans {facts['threats_found']} threats.", "On Tuesday morning, our computer support company changed the setting back. A complete antivirus check of each computer then found nothing.")) # Fact 6: the decisions she must take. pairs.append(("Lessons: verification step in every change ticket; every change in the maintenance calendar.", "Please approve two rules before Friday, October 16. First, every planned change must say how we will check that it worked. Second, every planned change goes into our maintenance calendar.")) # Fact 7: the law. pairs.append(("Private-sector Act s. 3.5-3.8 (amended by Law 25): no personal information accessed, used, communicated or lost; no CAI notice, no register entry.", "No personal information was seen, used, sent or lost. Québec law therefore does not require us to notify the Commission d'accès à l'information or anyone else.")) # Check every plain sentence: no abbreviation, no identifier, no sentence longer than the limit. problems = [] # Look at each plain sentence. for technical, plain in pairs: # Find the words that an owner would not understand. found = JARGON.findall(plain) # Every word found is a problem to fix. problems.extend(found) # Split the plain text into sentences and count the words of each one. for sentence in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", plain): # A sentence that is too long is also a problem. if len(sentence.split()) > MAX_WORDS: # Record the long sentence. problems.append(f"long sentence ({len(sentence.split())} words)") # Count the technical terms that the plain version replaced (the glossary shows the substitutions). replaced = sum(1 for technical, plain in pairs for row in glossary if row["term"] in technical and row["term"] not in plain) # Print the result of the check: zero problems is the goal. print(f" plain-language check: {len(problems)} problem(s){': ' + ', '.join(problems) if problems else ''}; {replaced} technical term(s) replaced by plain words; longest sentence {max(len(s.split()) for t, p in pairs for s in re.split(r'(?<=[.!?])\s+', p))} words (limit {MAX_WORDS})") # The label of the note, explained in plain words (TLP 2.0: in the header and the footer of the page). label = "TLP:AMBER+STRICT - internal to Atelier Nordik, do not forward." # Build the note: label, title, sender and date, then the five parts that Lab 3 Part D asks for. lines = [label, "", "# Antivirus updates on the three rendering computers", "", "To: the owner of Atelier Nordik. From: the monitoring technician. Tuesday, October 13, 1:00 pm.", ""] # Part 1: what happened (facts 1 to 3). lines += ["## What happened", pairs[0][1] + " " + pairs[1][1] + " " + pairs[2][1], ""] # Part 2: what it could have cost. lines += ["## What it could have cost", pairs[3][1], "", "- Who can see our information: not affected.", "- Whether our files are correct: not affected, but at risk during these four and a half days.", "- Whether we can use our computers and files: not affected.", ""] # Part 3: what was done. lines += ["## What was done", pairs[4][1] + " Everything we found is kept in the case file.", ""] # Part 4: the decisions. lines += ["## What we need from you", pairs[5][1], ""] # Part 5: what happens next. lines += ["## What happens next", pairs[6][1] + " We will review this change with our computer support company on Friday, October 16. Questions: call me.", ""] # The label again at the bottom of the page. lines += [label, ""] # Save the note. (OUT / "A09_owner_note.md").write_text("\n".join(lines), encoding="utf-8") # Give the pairs and the problems to the visual summary. return pairs, problems # STEP 5 - TECHNICAL ANNEX: details for the IT contractor, in the order of CCCS ITSAP.40.003.def step5_annex(facts): # Print the title of the step. print("STEP 5 - WRITE the technical annex (CCCS ITSAP.40.003 order) with evidence references") # Read the timeline of lesson 5.3 and the register of lesson 5.4. timeline, register = read_csv(OUT / "a09_timeline.csv"), read_csv(OUT / "evidence_register.csv") # Index the register by evidence identifier, to quote the hash next to each reference. sha = {row["evidence_id"]: row["sha256"][:12] for row in register} # The label of the annex (TLP 2.0): the contractor may share it inside its firm and, on a need-to-know basis, with its clients. label = "TLP:AMBER - the IT contractor may share this annex inside its firm and, on a need-to-know basis, with its clients." # Title and label of the annex. lines = [f"# Technical annex - {facts['case_id']} (alert A-09) - for the IT contractor", label, ""] # Phase 1 of ITSAP.40.003 used here: detection and analysis, with the key timeline rows. lines += ["## 1. Detection and analysis", f"Category: {facts['category']}. Root cause: {facts['root_cause']}. Tested and refuted: {facts['technique_tested']} (tactic TA0112 Defense Impairment, MITRE ATT&CK v19).", "", "| Time (EDT) | Evidence (file, line, SHA-256) | Record |", "|---|---|---|"] # Keep the key rows of the sequence of events. for row in timeline: # The same filter as the diagnosis record, so that both documents quote the same events. if re.search(r"event 2000, last success|CH-2026-090|FIRST failure|Alert A-09|LAST failure|does not exist", row["interpretation"]): # One table row with the exact reference: evidence identifier, file, line, hash. lines.append(f"| {row['time_edt']} | {row['evidence_id']} {row['file']} line {row['line']} ({sha[row['evidence_id']]}) | {row['interpretation']} |") # Phase 2: containment. lines += ["", "## 2. Containment", "Not required: no attacker; real-time protection stayed on. Risk accepted until the fix: definitions 4.5 days old on three workstations.", ""] # Phase 3: eradication. lines += ["## 3. Eradication", "Cause removed: policy Render-WS reverted to Microsoft Update (console audit 14:30:12Z, E-10). No malicious content found.", ""] # Phase 4: recovery, with the verification evidence. lines += ["## 4. Recovery (verified)", f"Forced update: definitions {facts['definitions_after_fix']} on the three workstations (E-09, event 2000). Full scans: {facts['threats_found']} threats (E-09 event 1001, E-11).", ""] # Phase 5: post-incident activities and lessons learned, in priority order. lines += ["## 5. Post-incident activities and lessons learned (review Fri 2026-10-16)"] + [f"{index}. {lesson}" for index, lesson in enumerate(facts["lessons"], start=1)] # The label again at the end of the annex. lines += ["", label] # Save the annex. (OUT / "A09_technical_annex.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8") # Print a confirmation. print(" annex: 5 phases, evidence quoted by file, line and hash") # STEP 6 - USERS, LAW and RECORD: the short message to the users, the legal decision, the communication record.def step6_record(people, decisions): # Print the title of the step. print("STEP 6 - WRITE the users' message, the legal decision and the communication record") # The label of the message (TLP 2.0 for e-mail: in the subject line and just before the information). label = "TLP:GREEN - you may share this message with colleagues, but not publicly." # The users' message: what happened in two sentences, that nothing is needed from them, whom to call. message = ["# TLP:GREEN - Rendering computers: antivirus fixed, nothing to do", "", label, "", "Hello,", "", "From Thursday evening to Tuesday morning, the antivirus of the three rendering computers could not get its updates. This came from a setting, not from an attack.", "", "It was fixed on Tuesday at 10:46 am, and a complete check found nothing. You do not need to do anything.", "", "If a computer shows an antivirus warning, do not close it: call the monitoring technician.", ""] # Save the users' message. (OUT / "A09_staff_message.md").write_text("\n".join(message), encoding="utf-8") # The legal decision, written even though no notice is required: the reasoning is the evidence. legal = ["# Notification decision - CASE-2026-016 (alert A-09)", "", "| Rule | Question | Answer | Consequence |", "|---|---|---|---|"] # One row per rule. legal += [f"| {d['rule']} | {d['question']} | {d['answer']} | {d['consequence']} |" for d in decisions] # Who took the decision and when. legal += ["", "Decision recorded by the technician, confirmed by the owner (person in charge of the protection of personal information, private-sector Act s. 3.1, as amended by Law 25), Tue 2026-10-13 13:00."] # Save the legal decision. (OUT / "A09_notification_decision.md").write_text("\n".join(legal) + "\n", encoding="utf-8") # The communication record: one row per stakeholder, with the status of the message. with open(OUT / "A09_communication_plan.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle: # A csv writer for the record. writer = csv.writer(handle) # Header of the record. writer.writerow(["stakeholder", "needs_to_know", "what_they_receive", "channel", "when", "sender", "tlp", "status"]) # One row per stakeholder. for person in people: # A message is "sent" for the people who need to know; for the others the reason is recorded. writer.writerow([person["stakeholder"], person["needs_to_know"], person["what_they_need"], person["channel"], person["when"], person["sender"], person["tlp"], "sent" if person["needs_to_know"] == "yes" else "not required (reason recorded)"]) # Print a confirmation with the file names. print(" saved: A09_owner_note.md, A09_technical_annex.md, A09_staff_message.md, A09_notification_decision.md, A09_communication_plan.csv") # The main block runs the six steps in order.if __name__ == "__main__": # Step 1: the facts. diagnosis = step1_facts() # Step 2: the law. legal_decisions = step2_notifications(diagnosis) # Step 3: the audiences. stakeholders = step3_audiences() # Step 4: the owner note, written and checked. sentence_pairs, issues = step4_owner_note(diagnosis) # Step 5: the technical annex. step5_annex(diagnosis) # Step 6: the users' message, the legal decision and the communication record. step6_record(stakeholders, legal_decisions)
Ready

The simulator replays the real output of the script, line by line, on the embedded evidence pack. Start and Pause control the replay; Pause keeps the position, and Start resumes from that step; Restart clears everything. While paused, click any line of the execution window to see which part of the code produced it.

Step-by-step explanation of build_report.py

  1. Preparation. The script defines the folders, the limit of 25 words per sentence, and a regular expression JARGON that finds what an owner would not understand: shared-folder paths, hexadecimal codes, identifiers such as WS-10-22 or CH-2026-090, and words in capital letters such as abbreviations.
  2. Step 1, facts. step1_facts() reads a09_diagnosis.json: every message will be written from these facts and from nothing else.
  3. Step 2, the law. step2_notifications() asks the four questions (Law 25, PIPEDA (Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act), Cyber Centre, police) and records each answer with its reason.
  4. Step 3, audiences. step3_audiences() reads stakeholders.csv and prints who is informed, through which channel, under which label, and who is not.
  5. Step 4, owner note. step4_owner_note() writes seven pairs (technical sentence, plain sentence) from the same facts, checks every plain sentence (0 problems, longest sentence 23 words) and assembles the five parts of the note.
  6. Step 5, annex. step5_annex() writes the five phases in ITSAP.40.003 (publication 40.003 of the Information Technology Security Awareness series of the Cyber Centre) order and quotes each key record with its file, line and the first 12 characters of the file's SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm, 256-bit) hash.
  7. Step 6, record. step6_record() writes the users' message, the notification decision and the communication record.

European Union: Directive 2013/40/EU on attacks against information systems (EUR-Lex)https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2013/40/ojEuropean Union rules on illegal access to information systems and illegal interception.
Spain: Ley Orgánica 10/1995, Código Penal (Boletín Oficial del Estado)https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1995-25444Spanish Criminal Code; article 197 bis covers illegal access to information systems.
